chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadah al-Raba'i from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said:

He was asked: Is it permissible for a place filled with earth (uneven/raised) to be made into a mosque? He said: 'If earth is thrown upon it that covers that unevenness and cuts off its wind/draft, then there is no harm, and that is because earth is purifying and the Sunnah has proceeded by it.'

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm (it is permissible)
key_terms.مَكَانٌ حَشٌّ: A place filled with or raised by earth (uneven ground)

ai.seo_question: Can a mosque be built on uneven ground covered with earth?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that a place with uneven or raised earth can be used as a mosque if earth is thrown upon it to cover the unevenness and block the wind. This is permissible because earth is considered ritually purifying (tahir) and this practice follows the established Sunnah. The ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the practicality of worship spaces, linking the physical act of leveling ground with the spiritual principle of earth's purifying nature, as derived from the Prophet's tradition.
